subject: Onboarding: Benchmarking & Acceptance — OrbitWave
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Ava Lin <ava@orbitwave.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding: Benchmarking & Acceptance — OrbitWave

Hi Ava —

Great to meet yesterday. Per our kickoff, attached is the initial benchmarking and acceptance plan so we can align on what constitutes a successful onboarding handoff. High-level summary:

- Acceptance targets (baseline): p50 latency <= 90ms, p95 latency <= 220ms for 1k token inference; sustained throughput target 150 QPS with 95% success rate under steady-state traffic.
- Spike test: 500 concurrent connections for 10 minutes to validate autoscaling and graceful degradation.
- Tail checks: 99th percentile latency under 600ms for 1k tokens.
- Test dataset: sample_prompt_set_v3.txt (attached) — production-ish mix of short/long prompts, average tokens ~420.
- Observability: we need read-only Datadog access + ingestion of trace context. Provide role/service account or temporary API key.
- Evidence: raw logs (JSON), testrun artifacts (csv), and a short findings doc. We will upload acceptance artifacts to the shared Drive folder (link below).

Proposed window: Wed 2028-06-07 18:00 UTC — Thu 2028-06-08 02:00 UTC (8 hour window). If that doesn't work for your ops team we can move to the following week.

Next steps / asks for you before we run:
1) Confirm the test window (or propose an alternative).
2) Provide a test API key for the dedicated sandbox and the CIDR(s) for where test traffic will originate (we run from our US-east pool and from an EU pool if you want cross-region testing).
3) Confirm any additional compliance requirements we should pause for test traffic (e.g., PII redaction, regional routing).

I've attached orbitwave_load_plan_v1.csv with sequences for concurrency ramps and a short runbook. Monica and Karthik — copying you for capacity coordination and to own the run.

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0120

Attachments: orbitwave_load_plan_v1.csv, sample_prompt_set_v3.txt

From: Ava Lin <ava@orbitwave.ai>

Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding: Benchmarking & Acceptance — OrbitWave

Thanks Sean — this looks good and very practical. A few clarifications from our side:

- The proposed acceptance numbers look reasonable but can you define whether the throughput target (150 QPS) assumes batching enabled on your side or raw single-request throughput? We typically test with both modes.
- We can provide a sandbox API key. Would you prefer a long-lived test key or a short-lived one we rotate on run day?
- For Datadog: we can grant a temporary read-only API key for the test window; I'll loop in Liam (ops) below to coordinate.
- Compliance: we do need to validate that PII is redacted in test logs for the third-party artifact export. Can you confirm Redwood's standard redaction policy for onboarding artifacts?

We can tentatively confirm the 2028-06-07 window but would like to shift the start by +1 hour to 19:00 UTC on your suggested date to avoid overlap with a deployment we have that evening.

-Ava
Product Ops | OrbitWave Inc
ava@orbitwave.ai

Hi Ava —

Thanks for the quick read. A couple operational points from Redwood CS/implementation:

- Throughput: the 150 QPS baseline assumes our default batching layer enabled (max batch size 8). We will also run an unbatched run to capture single-request latency for your SDK users.
- Redaction: Redwood will sanitize user-provided input in exported artifacts using our onboarding redaction pipeline (removes email addresses, credit-card-like sequences, and SSNs). We'll share a short redaction log with the artifacts. If OrbitWave needs a stricter policy for the acceptance package, let us know now so we can enable it before the run.
- Canary gating: we'll first run a low-intensity canary (30 min) and validate model fallback behavior and KV-cache warmup. If that looks good, we'll proceed to the full ramp.
- Runbook: I uploaded the canary_playbook and the run artifact template to the Drive folder. Link is in the shared links.

Sean — Karthik and I will own test orchestration and make sure we push logs into the shared folder in near-real time. Karthik, please confirm the agent and IP ranges we will use.

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the confirmation — updated plan below (and I've uploaded a small change-set of the load CSV that does a gentler ramp):

- Window: 2028-06-07 19:00 UTC — 2028-06-08 03:00 UTC (8 hrs).
- Canary: 19:00–19:30 UTC (low intensity).
- Ramp: 19:30–21:00 UTC (linear to 150 QPS).
- Sustained: 21:00–01:00 UTC (4 hours at target).
- Spike/chaos: 01:00–01:10 UTC (500 concurrent connections burst).
- Cooldown: 01:10–03:00 UTC (drain and artifact collection).

Acceptance criteria we will mark as PASS if both of these are met:
A) p95 latency <= 220ms during the sustained window (21:00–01:00 UTC) with batching enabled.
B) No more than 5% error rate for any 1-minute bucket during the sustained window.

Artifacts to deliver: raw request/response logs (JSON compressed), consolidated latency csv, and a 1-page executive summary with recommendation. We'll share the Drive link that houses the template.

- Sean: coordinate stakeholder updates and confirm HubSpot deal stage after acceptance.

- Karthik: run orchestration, provide agent IP range: 52.23.101.0/24 and 18.205.44.0/24.
- OrbitWave: provide sandbox key and Datadog read-only access.

Please reply here to confirm and we'll treat that as authorization to proceed.

Thanks,
Sean
